claims.statement: Directive (EU) 2023/970 requires specified gender pay-gap measures and recurring reporting by covered employer-size bands, beginning for larger employers in 2027.
The Directive provides for a joint pay assessment when an average gap of at least 5% in a worker category is unjustified and remains unremedied for six months.

contrary_evidence: Member-state transposition can differ and many employers already use compensation consultants or HR suites.
Reporting for the smallest covered band begins later than for larger employers.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: a privacy-safe library of job-normalisation mappings and tested neutral-factor diagnostics
fingerprint.customer: EU employers with structured payroll but limited internal compensation analytics
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: payroll bureaus, HRIS implementers, benefits brokers, and employment-law advisers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: secure cohort construction, required metrics, explainability, neutral-factor testing, and remediation simulation
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the employer or payroll bureau pays for recurring analysis and signed reporting packs
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a reporting deadline, worker request, unexplained category gap, promotion cycle, or compensation change

founder_fit: Highly aligned with statistics, explainable modelling, and corporate-data experience; bureau distribution limits founder-led selling and delivery can remain asynchronous.
risks: Sensitive payroll data demands strict security and minimisation.
Human legal and employee-representative review cannot be automated away.

structure.control_point: the management-confirmed pay analysis and remediation scenario used for reporting and worker responses
structure.critical_dependency: defensible job architecture and high-quality payroll/HRIS data joined without unlawful sensitive-data use

thesis: A privacy-preserving analytics engine can map payroll and job architecture into explainable equal-value cohorts, reproduce required gap measures, simulate neutral remediation, and retain management sign-off evidence. Payroll bureaus distribute it one-to-many; each payroll cycle, job change, information request, and reporting period refreshes the model.
title: Pay-Transparency Remediation Simulator Distributed by Payroll Bureaus
uncertainties: Whether employers prefer project consulting over software.
How reusable job mappings are across customers.
